items.summary: Vendor self-purchase: the blocked side (14.01.01 D-09 trailing clause, its edge-case row and buy-control row, and 14.08.01 edge case 13) was stale drift against the canonical decision in the file that owns entitlement issuance — 14.02.01 D-11 (permitted and flagged), backed by its rejected trade-off DT-10. Rewrote the four drifted locations to state the canonical rule and cite it; left the residual buy-control-placement sub-question tracked as 14.01.01 Q-07.
items.canonicalSource: 14.02-licensing-activation-entitlement/14.02.01-licence-issuance-entitlement-record.md:201 (D-11) — "**Self-purchase is permitted and flagged** at issuance (holder principal == the product's vendor principal, or an org the vendor controls); downstream excludes it from payout, sales rank, reviews and loyalty accrual"; grounded at :158 (DT-10) — "A vendor buying their own product is therefore **normal** and cannot be blocked."
canonicalEvidence: 14.02.01-licence-issuance-entitlement-record.md:201 — D-11, the numbered decision in the file that owns licence issuance and entitlement records; i.e. the file that owns whether a purchase mints an entitlement at all.

14.02.01-licence-issuance-entitlement-record.md:158 — DT-10, a fully worked rejected trade-off that considered and named all three answers ('the answer is neither "block" nor "ignore" but flag at issuance'). No comparable deliberation exists on the blocked side.

meta/personas.md:30-34 — the Structural Fact DT-10 cites, verified verbatim: 'one human simultaneously holds several professional roles ... A persona model of "user has a role" is wrong for this product.'
14.04-sound-content-catalogs/14.04.01-sample-loop-pack-catalog.md:174 — 'Not blocked - blocking it teaches vendors to use a second account, which is worse.'
14.03-delivery-versioning-library/14.03.03-licence-portal-purchased-library.md:192 — 'Buying your own product is normal (testing the buyer flow) and is not a signal by itself'
14.09-digital-refunds-revocation/14.09.02-digital-refund-eligibility-adjudication.md:169 — routes a self-purchase refund to fraud review, which presupposes the purchase exists
digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:32 (CX-21), :402, :411 — the domain reconciliation surface presupposes self-purchases exist and must be excluded from earnings
items.whyMechanicalNotOwner: The blocked side looks like a second numbered decision but is not one on this concept. 14.01.01 D-09's subject is the lens ('vendor lens with a View as buyer toggle; never a role picker'); 'Self-purchase is blocked on the same surface' was a trailing clause appended to a decision about something else — and it contradicted the very personas.md Structural Fact that D-09's own rationale invokes. 14.08.01 edge case 13 was not an independent decision either: it cited 14.01.01 D-09 as its authority, making it a downstream restatement of the drifted clause. Against that, 14.02.01 D-11 is the owning file's numbered decision with a worked rejected alternative, and seven further locations across five sub-domains align with it. The blocked reading also left a hole the verifier confirmed: its stated substitute, 14.02.05 D-16, covers only a vendor placing their own product into a project, never a purchase — so under the blocked reading the purchase path had no defined entitlement at all, while the permitted reading is complete and internally consistent domain-wide. One-sided drift, not a live collision.
items.fixApplied: Four edits, all on the drifted side; the canonical source (14.02.01) was not touched. (1) 14.01.01:76 buy-control table, vendor row — was 'No buy control. Edit + View as buyer (D-09)', now 'Edit + View as buyer (D-09); the buy control renders under the buyer lens — self-purchase is permitted and flagged, not blocked (14.02.01 D-11)'. (2) 14.01.01:127 edge case — retitled 'Vendor buys their own listing' and rewritten to state permitted-and-flagged with the downstream exclusions (payout 14.10, sales rank, review eligibility, loyalty accrual 14.07.05) and the second-account argument from 14.04.01; outcome column now states the ordinary buy control under View as buyer, nothing said to the buyer, and the vendor dashboard showing the sale excluded with its reason (14.02.01:105). (3) 14.01.01:213 D-09 — the trailing clause 'Self-purchase is blocked on the same surface (sales-rank gaming, laundering)' replaced with an explicit non-block that keeps D-09's lens decision intact and routes the sales-rank/laundering exposure to flagging at issuance per 14.02.01 D-11/DT-10. (4) 14.08.01:134 edge case 13 — rewritten to permitted-and-flagged citing 14.02.01 D-11/DT-10, with the per-line evaluation rule, and 14.02.05 D-16 corrected from 'instead' to what it actually covers: project placement, a distinct case that is not a purchase.

trackedQuestionAdded.question: Does the vendor lens surface a buy control directly, or only under `View as buyer`?
trackedQuestionAdded.why: The permission is settled by 14.02.01 D-11 and the buyer lens shows the control by definition, since `View as buyer` means 'see this listing as a customer' (D-09). What neither 14.01 nor 14.02 states is whether the default vendor lens renders `Buy — £X` beside `Edit`. This is a surface call, not a policy call, and stating it either way would have invented product behaviour.
